description: How telecommunication networks carry voice and data at scale: an overview of network structure, switching and signalling, transmission systems, optical-fibre and satellite communication, traffic engineering, and the regulation of telecommunications. Taught with browser-based simulations of links, switches and traffic loads, so students dimension networks, model blocking and trace a call or packet across the network without physical equipment.
modelledOn: Rappaport, Wireless Communications: Principles and Practice
ITU-T recommendations and the ITU radio regulations
outcomes: Describe the structure of a telecommunication network from access to core.
Explain circuit and packet switching and the signalling that sets up and controls connections.
Analyse transmission systems in terms of bandwidth, multiplexing, modulation and impairments.
Explain optical-fibre and satellite links and when each is the right choice.
Apply traffic engineering to dimension a network and estimate blocking and quality of service.
Describe how telecommunications are regulated and how spectrum and licensing are managed.

units.title: Telecommunication networks overview
topics: The anatomy of a network: access, aggregation, core and interconnection
A brief history from the telegraph and telephone to mobile and all-IP networks
Analogue versus digital; bandwidth, bit rate and the Nyquist and Shannon limits
Standards and layering; the roles of the ITU, IEEE and regional bodies
Ghana's telecom landscape: the mobile operators, mobile money and the national backbone

units.title: Switching and signalling
topics: Circuit, message and packet switching and the trade-offs between them
Space- and time-division switching inside a switch fabric
Signalling: in-band versus out-of-band and the common-channel signalling system
Call set-up, routing and teardown; numbering and addressing plans
The move from circuit-switched telephony to voice over IP and softswitches

units.title: Transmission systems
topics: Transmission media: copper pair, coaxial, radio and fibre and their characteristics
Impairments: attenuation, noise, distortion and the link budget
Modulation: amplitude, frequency, phase and quadrature schemes
Multiplexing: frequency-, time-, wavelength- and code-division
Digital transmission hierarchies and the synchronous optical and digital hierarchies
Error detection and correction on a link

units.title: Optical fibre communication
topics: Light guiding in fibre: total internal reflection, single- and multi-mode fibre
Sources, detectors and the optical link budget; attenuation and dispersion windows
Wavelength-division multiplexing and optical amplifiers for long-haul capacity
Submarine cable systems and the West Africa cables that carry the region's traffic
Fibre to the home and the access network; resilience when a cable is cut

units.title: Wireless and mobile transmission
topics: Radio propagation: path loss, fading, multipath and interference
Cellular principles: cells, frequency reuse, handover and capacity
Generations of mobile networks and their air interfaces in brief
Spectrum as a scarce resource and why it is licensed
Mobile coverage realities in rural Ghana and the economics of extending it

units.title: Satellite communication
topics: Orbits: geostationary, medium and low earth orbit and their latency and coverage trade-offs
The satellite link: uplink, downlink, transponders and the ground segment
Link budget, rain fade and frequency bands
Applications: backhaul for remote areas, broadcasting and new low-earth-orbit broadband
When satellite is the right choice for underserved communities

units.title: Traffic engineering
topics: Offered traffic, the erlang and grade of service
The Erlang-B and Erlang-C models for blocking and queued systems
Dimensioning circuits and channels for a target blocking probability
Queueing basics for packet networks: utilisation, delay and loss
Quality of service, congestion and admission control
Dimensioning a mobile cell or a data link under a given load in the simulator

units.title: Regulation of telecommunications
topics: Why telecoms are regulated: scarce spectrum, natural monopoly and universal service
Licensing, interconnection and number portability
Spectrum management and the ITU's role in international coordination
Ghana's National Communications Authority: licensing, SIM registration and consumer protection
Pricing, competition and universal-access funds for underserved areas
Capstone: plan and dimension a regulated access network for a Ghanaian district

schedule.title: The anatomy of a network and digital signals
schedule.exercise: Compute the Shannon capacity of a channel given bandwidth and signal-to-noise ratio, and explain what changing each input does to the limit.

tasks.title: Compute the Nyquist sampling rate and the Shannon capacity for three given bandwidth and noise scenarios, and compare the results
Draw the access, aggregation, core and interconnection layers for a described national network, labelling where a household's traffic enters each layer
Plot an analogue sine wave and its digitised, quantised version side by side, and measure the quantisation error introduced

schedule.title: Standards and Ghana's telecom landscape
schedule.exercise: Write a short note on why layered standards from bodies like the ITU and IEEE let equipment from different vendors interoperate.

tasks.title: Map a described communication exchange onto a layered protocol stack and identify which layer a stated standard belongs to
Draw a diagram of Ghana's mobile operators, mobile money services and the national backbone, and mark where an outage would affect the most users
Build a simple layered network in the simulator and show that two correctly layered devices interoperate while a mismatched one fails

schedule.title: Switching and signalling
schedule.exercise: Compare circuit, message and packet switching for a voice call and an email, and justify which switching type suits each.

tasks.title: Set up a simulated circuit-switched call path and a packet-switched data path between the same two endpoints and compare the delay of each
Trace an in-band and an out-of-band signalling exchange for a call setup, and explain why separating signalling from voice improved reliability
Diagram a space-division and a time-division switch fabric for the same four inputs and outputs and compare how each connects a given pair

schedule.title: Call routing and the move to VoIP
schedule.exercise: Explain, with a diagram, the three phases of a telephone call (set-up, routing, teardown) and how they differ for a VoIP call using a softswitch.

tasks.title: Trace call set-up, routing and teardown for a simulated call between two numbering plan addresses, and identify the role of each signalling message
Build a simple VoIP path through a softswitch and compare its signalling steps with the equivalent circuit-switched call
Design a numbering and addressing plan for a small telecom network with three exchanges, and resolve a numbering conflict between two of them

schedule.title: Transmission media and impairments
schedule.exercise: Compute the link budget for a given copper, radio and fibre link and determine which impairment dominates each.

tasks.title: Compare the bandwidth and attenuation characteristics of copper, coaxial and fibre links over a given distance and recommend one for a scenario
Compute a link budget for a radio link given transmit power, path loss and receiver sensitivity, and determine if it closes
Plot the constellation of an ASK, FSK and PSK modulated signal and identify which one is more robust to a given noise level

schedule.title: Multiplexing and digital hierarchies
schedule.exercise: Explain with a diagram how frequency-, time- and wavelength-division multiplexing each let multiple signals share one medium.

tasks.title: Simulate four signals multiplexed by time-division onto one channel and demultiplexed back, and verify no signal is lost or mixed with another
Introduce a bit error into a transmitted codeword and show a simple error-detecting code catches it, then show an error-correcting code repairs it
Diagram the hierarchy levels of a synchronous digital transmission system and show how four lower-rate streams combine into one higher-rate stream

schedule.title: Fibre optics
schedule.exercise: Compute the optical link budget for a given fibre length, attenuation and connector loss, and state whether a repeater is needed.

tasks.title: Explain total internal reflection with a ray diagram for single-mode and multi-mode fibre, and compute the critical angle for given refractive indices
Compute an optical link budget for a given fibre run with stated attenuation and connector losses, and determine the margin at the receiver
Compare the capacity gain from adding wavelength-division multiplexing to a single fibre link against adding a second fibre

schedule.title: Submarine cables and access networks
schedule.exercise: Write a short resilience plan for a country whose main submarine cable is cut, listing the backup options and their trade-offs.

tasks.title: Draw a map of the West Africa submarine cable systems and identify which countries would be most affected if one cable were cut
Design a fibre-to-the-home access network for a described neighbourhood, and compare its resilience with a single shared feeder line
Estimate the capacity loss and rerouting delay for a country when one submarine cable is cut, given the remaining cable capacities

schedule.title: Radio propagation and cellular principles
schedule.exercise: Explain frequency reuse with a worked example of cluster size, and compute the reuse distance for a given cell radius.

tasks.title: Compute received signal strength using a log-distance path loss model for three distances and compare with a measured value
Design a frequency reuse pattern for a described cluster of cells and compute the reuse distance for a given cell radius
Plan a cellular coverage layout for rural Ghana balancing tower cost against the number of towers needed for a stated coverage target

schedule.title: Satellite communication
schedule.exercise: Compare GEO, MEO and LEO orbits for a rural broadband service, using a table of latency, coverage and cost trade-offs.

tasks.title: Compute the round-trip latency for a GEO, a MEO and a LEO satellite link and explain why the difference matters for a voice call
Compute a satellite link budget including rain fade for a given frequency band and determine the margin under clear and rainy conditions
Decide whether satellite, fibre or cellular backhaul best serves a described underserved community, and justify the choice against cost and latency

schedule.title: Traffic engineering
schedule.exercise: Use the Erlang B formula to compute the number of trunks needed for a given offered traffic and blocking probability target.

tasks.title: Compute offered traffic in erlangs from a given call volume and holding time, and interpret what the number means for trunk planning
Use the Erlang B formula to find the number of circuits needed for a given traffic load and a 2 percent blocking probability
Dimension the circuits for a rural exchange given a forecast traffic increase, and determine how many extra circuits a 5 percent blocking target needs

schedule.title: Packet queueing and quality of service
schedule.exercise: Explain how a queuing delay model differs from the circuit-switched blocking model, and state which one applies to a congested data link.

tasks.title: Model a packet queue with a given arrival rate and service rate, and compute the utilisation and average delay
Configure a QoS policy on a simulated congested link so voice traffic is prioritised over bulk data, and measure the delay improvement
Dimension a mobile cell's data channels for a target blocking probability under a given traffic load, and verify the chosen capacity in the simulator

schedule.title: Regulation and the capstone network plan
schedule.exercise: Write a short justification of why spectrum is licensed and why unlicensed bands like Wi-Fi exist alongside it.

tasks.title: Compare licensing, interconnection and number portability rules for a described new entrant operator and identify the biggest regulatory hurdle
Evaluate how Ghana's National Communications Authority rules on SIM registration and consumer protection would apply to a described new service
Plan and dimension a regulated access network for a Ghanaian district, choosing media, capacity and coverage, and justify the plan against a stated budget and coverage target
